# Caesium Command Line Tools

**caesiumclt** is a powerful command-line tool for image compression that delivers exceptional results
with minimal effort. Whether you need pixel-perfect lossless compression or aggressive size reduction, caesiumclt has
you covered.

## ✨ Features

- **Multiple Compression Modes**
    - 🔍 Quality-based lossy compression
    - 💎 Lossless compression—preserve image quality while reducing size
    - 📏 Maximum size compression - target specific file sizes

- **Advanced Image Processing**
    - 📐 Resize images with multiple options (width, height, long/short edge)
    - 🔄 Convert between formats (JPEG, PNG, WebP)
    - 🏷️ EXIF metadata preservation

- **Workflow Optimization**
    - *️⃣ Recursive directory compression
    - 📁 Folder structure preservation
    - 🕒 File timestamp preservation
    - 📝 Custom suffix for output files
    - ⚡ Fast and customizable multithreaded processing

### Supported Formats

| Format   | Lossy | Lossless |
|----------|:-----:|:--------:|
| **JPEG** |   ✅   |    ✅     |
| **PNG**  |   ✅   |    ✅     |
| **WebP** |   ✅   |    ✅     |
| **GIF**  |   ✅   |    ❌     |

## 🚀 Getting Started

### Binaries

Download the latest binaries from the [release page](https://github.com/Lymphatus/caesium-clt/releases).

**Supported platforms:**

- Windows (x86_64)
- macOS (x86_64/aarch64)
- Linux (x86_64/aarch64)

## 📖 Usage

### Command-Line Options

#### Compression (at least one is required)

- `-q, --quality <QUALITY>`  
  Sets compression quality between 0 and 100. Higher the value, better the quality and bigger the file size.
- `--lossless`  
  Perform lossless compression. Some file formats may not support this or result in bigger file sizes.
- `--max-size <MAX_SIZE>`  
  Attempts to compress the image to the nearest size in bytes without exceeding it. If the requested size is too small,
  it will output the smallest possible result.

#### Advanced compression

- `--jpeg-chroma-subsampling <JPEG_CHROMA_SUBSAMPLING>`  
  Sets the chroma subsampling for JPEG files. Possible values are:
    - `4:4:4`
    - `4:2:2`
    - `4:2:0`
    - `4:1:1`
    - `auto`

- `--jpeg-baseline`  
  Forces the output to be in baseline JPEG format instead of progressive.

- `--png-opt-level <PNG_OPT_LEVEL>`  
  Sets the optimization level for PNG files. Higher values result in better compression but take longer to complete.
  Possible values are between 0 and 6. Default is 3.
- `--zopfli`  
  Use zopfli when optimizing PNG files. It may take a very long time to complete.

#### Metadata

- `-e, --exif`  
  Keeps EXIF metadata info during compression, if present. This can slightly increase the output file size.
- `--keep-dates`  
  Keeps the original last modified and last accessed date information, if possible.
- `--strip-icc`  
  Strips all ICC profile information on JPG, regardless of `-e` flag.

#### Resizing

- `--width <WIDTH>`  
  Sets the width of the output image. If height is not set, it will preserve the aspect ratio. Can't be used with
  `--long-edge` or `--short-edge`.
- `--height <HEIGHT>`  
  Sets the height of the output image. If width is not set, it will preserve the aspect ratio. Can't be used with
  `--long-edge` or `--short-edge`.
- `--long-edge <LONG_EDGE>`  
  Sets the size of the longest edge of the image. It is aware of rotation metadata. Can't be used with `--width` or
  `--height` or `--short-edge`.
- `--short-edge <SHORT_EDGE>`  
  Sets the size of the shortest edge of the image. It is aware of rotation metadata. Can't be used with `--width` or
  `--height` or `--long-edge`.
- `--no-upscale`  
  Prevent upscaling the image when resizing

#### Destination

- `-o, --output <OUTPUT>`  
  Sets the output folder. If the folder does not exist, it will be created. Can't be used with `--same-folder-as-input`.
- `--same-folder-as-input`  
  Sets the output folder to be the same as the input folder. WARNING: this can potentially overwrite the original files
  if a suffix is not set. Overwritten files CANNOT be recovered.
- `--suffix <SUFFIX>`  
  Adds a suffix to the output filename, before the file extension.
- `-S, --keep-structure`  
  Preserves the folder tree structure of the input files. Can be used only with `-R`.

    - `all`: Always overwrite
    - `never`: Never overwrite
    - `bigger`: Overwrite only if the file to be overwritten is bigger
- `--min-savings <MIN_SAVINGS>`

- `--min-savings <MIN_SAVINGS>`  
  Skip writing the output file if the compression savings are below the specified threshold.
  This is useful to prevent repeated re-compression from degrading image quality.  
  Supported formats:
    - Percentage (supports decimals): `10%`, `1.5%`, `0.1%`
    - Size with unit: `100KB`, `1MB`, `500KiB`
    - Plain number (interpreted as bytes): `1000`, `50000`
- `--format <FORMAT>`  
  Converts the original image to the selected format. Possible values are:
    - `jpeg`
    - `png`
    - `webp`
    - `original` (default, no changes)

#### Other

- `-R, --recursive`  
  If the input is a folder, scan its subfolders too.
- `-d, --dry-run`  
  Do not write output files, only simulate the process.
- `--threads <THREADS>`  
  Specify the number of parallel jobs. The maximum is the number of processors available. `0` means that the application
  will try to guess the maximum number of parallel jobs available. Default is `0`.
- `-Q, --quiet`  
  Suppress all output. Overrides `--verbose`.
- `--verbose <VERBOSE>`  
  Select how much output you want to see. Possible values are:
    - `0`: Suppress all output
    - `1`: Show only progress and final results
    - `2`: Show also skipped and error messages
    - `3`: Print all
- `-h, --help`  
  Print help. A summary can be seen with `-h`.
- `-V, --version`  
  Print version.

### Examples

**Lossless compression:**

```bash
# Compress a single image
$ caesiumclt --lossless -o output/ image.jpg

# Compress with metadata preservation
$ caesiumclt --lossless -e --keep-dates -o output/ image.jpg

# Compress a directory recursively
$ caesiumclt --lossless -R -o output/ Pictures

# Preserve folder structure
$ caesiumclt --lossless -RS -o output/ Pictures
```

**Lossy compression:**

```bash
# Compress with quality setting
$ caesiumclt -q 80 -o output/ image.jpg

# Compress multiple images with a specific quality
$ caesiumclt -q 75 -o output/ image1.jpg image2.png image3.webp

# Compress with suffix to avoid overwriting originals
$ caesiumclt -q 85 --suffix _compressed --same-folder-as-input image.jpg
```

**Format conversion:**

```bash
# Convert images to WebP format with quality setting
$ caesiumclt -q 85 --format webp -o output/ Pictures/*.jpg

# Convert PNG to JPEG with maximum quality
$ caesiumclt -q 100 --format jpeg -o output/ image.png
```

**Resizing options:**

```bash
# Resize to specific width (maintaining aspect ratio)
$ caesiumclt --lossless --width 1920 -o output/ image.jpg

# Resize to specific height (maintaining aspect ratio)
$ caesiumclt -q 90 --height 1080 -o output/ image.jpg

# Resize by longest edge (useful for mixed portrait/landscape photos)
$ caesiumclt -q 85 --long-edge 1500 -o output/ Pictures/*.jpg

# Resize by shortest edge
```

def dqt(path):
 data=open(path,'rb').read(); i=2
 tables={}
 while i<len(data):
  m=data[i+1]
  if m==0xDA: break
  ln=struct.unpack('>H',data[i+2:i+4])[0]; seg=data[i+4:i+2+ln]

import zlib,struct,os,random
def chunk(t,d):
 return struct.pack('>I',len(d))+t+d+struct.pack('>I',zlib.crc32(t+d)&0xffffffff)
def write_png(path,w,h,ct,pixels,bitd=8,extra=[],level=6,filter_type=0,plte=None,trns=None,inter=0):
 # pixels: bytes rows without filter, packed according spec precomputed by caller rowbytes
 rowlen=len(pixels)//h
 raw=b''.join(bytes([filter_type])+pixels[y*rowlen:(y+1)*rowlen] for y in range(h))
 data=b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n'
 data+=chunk(b'IHDR',struct.pack('>IIBBBBB',w,h,bitd,ct,0,0,inter))
 for t,d in extra:
  if t==b'PLTE': continue
  data+=chunk(t,d)
 if plte: data+=chunk(b'PLTE',plte)
 if trns: data+=chunk(b'tRNS',trns)
 data+=chunk(b'IDAT',zlib.compress(raw,level))
 data+=chunk(b'IEND',b'')
 open(path,'wb').write(data)
os.makedirs('/tmp/gen',exist_ok=True)
random.seed(1)
# small RGB gradient 8x8 unique colors
pix=bytearray()
for y in range(8):
 for x in range(8): pix+=bytes([x*30,y*30, (x+y)*15])
write_png('/tmp/gen/rgb8.png',8,8,2,bytes(pix),level=0)
# RGBA with alpha
pix=bytearray()
for y in range(8):
 for x in range(8): pix+=bytes([x*30,y*30,128, 255 if (x+y)%2 else 100])
write_png('/tmp/gen/rgba8.png',8,8,6,bytes(pix),level=0)
# RGBA fully opaque
pix=bytearray()
for y in range(8):
 for x in range(8): pix+=bytes([x*30,y*30,128,255])
write_png('/tmp/gen/rgba_opaque.png',8,8,6,bytes(pix))
# gray
pix=bytes([x*16 for y in range(16) for x in range(16)])
write_png('/tmp/gen/gray.png',16,16,0,pix)
# gray+alpha
pix=bytearray()
for i in range(256): pix+=bytes([i, 200])
write_png('/tmp/gen/graya.png',16,16,4,bytes(pix))
# palette 3 colors indices
pix=bytes([(x+y)%3 for y in range(10) for x in range(10)])
write_png('/tmp/gen/pal.png',10,10,3,pix,bitd=8,plte=bytes([255,0,0,0,255,0,0,0,255]),trns=bytes([128,255,255]))
# RGB with only 3 colors (reducible to palette)
pix=bytearray()
cols=[(255,0,0),(0,255,0),(0,0,255)]
for y in range(10):
 for x in range(10): pix+=bytes(cols[(x+y)%3])
write_png('/tmp/gen/rgb3col.png',10,10,2,bytes(pix))
# RGB grayscale content
pix=bytearray()
for y in range(10):
 for x in range(10): v=(x*20+y*5)%256; pix+=bytes([v,v,v])
write_png('/tmp/gen/rgbgray.png',10,10,2,bytes(pix))
# 16-bit RGB (values in high byte dup)
pix=bytearray()
for y in range(4):
 for x in range(4):
  for v in [x*50,y*50,100]: pix+=struct.pack('>H',v*257)
write_png('/tmp/gen/rgb16.png',4,4,2,bytes(pix),bitd=16)
# 16-bit true values not 8-bit reducible
pix=bytearray()
for y in range(4):
 for x in range(4):
  for v in [x*1000,y*2000,30000]: pix+=struct.pack('>H',v)
write_png('/tmp/gen/rgb16b.png',4,4,2,bytes(pix),bitd=16)
# extra chunks
extra=[(b'tEXt',b'Title\x00Hello'),(b'gAMA',struct.pack('>I',45455)),(b'cHRM',b'\x00'*32),(b'tIME',struct.pack('>HBBBBB',2020,1,2,3,4,5)),(b'pHYs',struct.pack('>IIB',2835,2835,1)),(b'eXIf',b'MM\x00*\x00\x00\x00\x08\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00')]
write_png('/tmp/gen/extra.png',8,8,2,bytes([128]*8*8*3),extra=extra)
# large random RGB 64x64 level0 (optimizable)
pix=bytes(random.randrange(256) for _ in range(64*64*3))
write_png('/tmp/gen/random64.png',64,64,2,pix,level=0)

import struct
def getdims(path):
 d=open(path,'rb').read()
 if d[:8]==b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n': return f"{struct.unpack('>I',d[16:20])[0]}x{struct.unpack('>I',d[20:24])[0]}"
 if d[:2]==b'\xff\xd8':
  i=2
  while i<len(d):
   m=d[i+1]
   if m==0xDA: break
   ln=struct.unpack('>H',d[i+2:i+4])[0]
   if m in (0xC0,0xC1,0xC2): return f"{struct.unpack('>H',d[i+7:i+9])[0]}x{struct.unpack('>H',d[i+5:i+7])[0]}"
   i+=2+ln
 if d[:3]==b'GIF': return f"{struct.unpack('<H',d[6:8])[0]}x{struct.unpack('<H',d[8:10])[0]}"
 if d[:4]==b'RIFF':
  typ=d[12:16]
  if typ==b'VP8 ': return f"{struct.unpack('<H',d[26:28])[0]&0x3fff}x{struct.unpack('<H',d[28:30])[0]&0x3fff}"
  if typ==b'VP8L':
   bits=struct.unpack('<I',d[21:25])[0]; return f"{(bits&0x3fff)+1}x{((bits>>14)&0x3fff)+1}"
  if typ==b'VP8X':
   z=b'\x00'; return f"{struct.unpack('<I',d[24:27]+z)[0]+1}x{struct.unpack('<I',d[27:30]+z)[0]+1}"
 if d[:2]==b'II':

import struct,sys
for path in sys.argv[1:]:
 d=open(path,'rb').read(); print(path,len(d),d[:6],struct.unpack('<HHBB',d[6:13]))
 i=13; packed=d[10]
 if packed&128:
  gct=3*(2**((packed&7)+1)); print(' GCT bytes',gct); i+=gct
 fr=0
 while i<len(d):
  b=d[i]
  if b==0x21:
   lab=d[i+1]; print(f' ext label {lab:02x} at {i}', end='')
   i+=2
   if lab==0xf9:
    sz=d[i]; print(' GCE',d[i:i+1+sz].hex(), 'packed',d[i+1],'delay',struct.unpack('<H',d[i+2:i+4])[0],'transidx',d[i+4]); i+=1+sz+1
   else:
    # app ext first block 11 etc then subblocks
    chunks=[]
    while True:
     sz=d[i]; i+=1
     if sz==0: break
     chunks.append(d[i:i+sz]); i+=sz
    print(' data',chunks[:3])
  elif b==0x2c:
   x,y,w,h,ipacked=struct.unpack('<HHHHB',d[i+1:i+10]); i+=10
   lct=0
   if ipacked&128: lct=3*(2**((ipacked&7)+1)); i+=lct
   print(f' frame{fr} xy={x},{y} {w}x{h} packed={ipacked:08b} lctbytes={lct} mincode={d[i]}'); fr+=1; i+=1
   total=0
   while True:
    sz=d[i]; i+=1
    if sz==0: break
    total+=sz; i+=sz
   print('  compressed bytes',total)
  elif b==0x3b: print(' trailer'); break
  else: print(' unknown',hex(b),'at',i); break

python3 << 'PY'
import struct
# Take orient6.webp, parse chunks and insert XMP chunk + set VP8X flag bit XMP (0x04?) VP8X flags byte: reserved 2 bits, ICC 0x20, alpha0x10, exif0x08, xmp0x04, anim0x02
d=open('/tmp/gen/orient6.webp','rb').read()
# append XMP chunk before end and adjust RIFF size and VP8X flags
xmp=b'<x:xmpmeta>hello</x:xmpmeta>'
chunk=b'XMP '+struct.pack('<I',len(xmp))+xmp+(b'\x00' if len(xmp)%2 else b'')
out=bytearray(d+chunk)
out[4:8]=struct.pack('<I',len(out)-8)
out[20]=out[20]|0x04
open('/tmp/gen/metadata.webp','wb').write(out)
PY
python3 /tmp/inspect.py /tmp/gen/metadata.webp
for mode in "-q 80" "-q 80 -e" "--lossless" "--lossless -e"; do rm -rf /tmp/out; ./executable $mode -o /tmp/out /tmp/gen/metadata.webp >/dev/null; echo "WEBP same $mode"; python3 /tmp/inspect.py /tmp/out/metadata.webp; done

  i+=2+ln

   283	pub struct Quantized {

   294	impl ColorBox {
   295	    fn mean_and_error(&self) -> ([f64; 4], f64) {
   296	        // Premultiplied mean for the palette colour and straight mean for error.
   297	        let mut sums = [0f64; 4];
   298	        let mut sum_a = 0f64;
   299	        let mut prem = [0f64; 3];
   300	        for (c, n) in &self.colors {
   301	            let n = *n as f64;
   302	            for k in 0..4 { sums[k] += c[k] as f64 * n; }
   303	            let a = c[3] as f64 / 255.0;
   304	            sum_a += c[3] as f64 * n;
   305	            for k in 0..3 { prem[k] += c[k] as f64 * a * n; }
   306	        }
   307	        let total = self.total.max(1) as f64;
   308	        let straight = [sums[0] / total, sums[1] / total, sums[2] / total, sums[3] / total];

   310	        for (c, n) in &self.colors {
   311	            let mut d = 0f64;
   312	            for k in 0..4 { let diff = c[k] as f64 - straight[k]; d += diff * diff; }
   313	            err += d * *n as f64;
   314	        }

   316	        let mean = if sum_a > 0.0 {
   317	            [prem[0] * 255.0 / sum_a, prem[1] * 255.0 / sum_a, prem[2] * 255.0 / sum_a, alpha]
   318	        } else { straight };

   323	fn split_box(b: ColorBox) -> Vec<ColorBox> {

        .collect();
    let iterations = if colors.len() <= 20_000 {
        16
    } else if colors.len() <= 100_000 {
        6
    } else {
        0
    };
    if iterations == 0 {
        return init;
    }
    let premult = |c: [f32; 4]| -> [f32; 4] {
        let a = c[3] / 255.0;
        [c[0] * a, c[1] * a, c[2] * a, c[3]]
    };
    let mut assignment: Vec<usize> = vec![0; colors.len()];
    for _ in 0..iterations {
        let center_pm: Vec<[f32; 4]> = centers.iter().map(|c| premult(*c)).collect();
        let mut changed = false;
        let mut worst_dist = -1.0f32;
        let mut worst_idx = 0usize;
        for (i, (c, _)) in colors.iter().enumerate() {
            let cp = premult([c[0] as f32, c[1] as f32, c[2] as f32, c[3] as f32]);
            let mut best = 0usize;
            let mut bestd = f32::INFINITY;
            for (j, cen) in center_pm.iter().enumerate() {
                let d = (cp[0] - cen[0]).powi(2)
                    + (cp[1] - cen[1]).powi(2)
                    + (cp[2] - cen[2]).powi(2)
                    + (cp[3] - cen[3]).powi(2);
                if d < bestd {
                    bestd = d;
                    best = j;
                }
            }
            if assignment[i] != best {
                changed = true;
                assignment[i] = best;
            }
            if bestd > worst_dist {
                worst_dist = bestd;
                worst_idx = i;
            }
        }
        // Recompute centres.
        let mut sums = vec![[0f64; 4]; k]; // premultiplied rgb sums + alpha sum
        let mut counts = vec![0f64; k];
        for (i, (c, n)) in colors.iter().enumerate() {
            let a = c[3] as f64 / 255.0;
            let j = assignment[i];
            let wgt = *n as f64;
            sums[j][0] += c[0] as f64 * a * wgt;
            sums[j][1] += c[1] as f64 * a * wgt;
            sums[j][2] += c[2] as f64 * a * wgt;
            sums[j][3] += c[3] as f64 * wgt;
            counts[j] += wgt;
        }
        for j in 0..k {
            if counts[j] > 0.0 {
                let alpha = sums[j][3] / counts[j];
                if sums[j][3] > 0.0 {
                    centers[j] = [
                        (sums[j][0] * 255.0 / sums[j][3]) as f32,
                        (sums[j][1] * 255.0 / sums[j][3]) as f32,
                        (sums[j][2] * 255.0 / sums[j][3]) as f32,
                        alpha as f32,
                    ];
                } else {
                    centers[j][3] = 0.0;
                }
            } else {
                // Re-seed an empty cluster at the worst-served colour.
                let c = colors[worst_idx].0;
                centers[j] = [c[0] as f32, c[1] as f32, c[2] as f32, c[3] as f32];
                changed = true;
            }
        }
        if !changed {
            break;
        }
    }
    let mut out: Vec<[u8; 4]> = Vec::new();
    for c in centers {
        let v = [
            c[0].clamp(0.0, 255.0).round() as u8,
            c[1].clamp(0.0, 255.0).round() as u8,
            c[2].clamp(0.0, 255.0).round() as u8,
            c[3].clamp(0.0, 255.0).round() as u8,
        ];
        if !out.contains(&v) {
            out.push(v);
        }
    }
    out
}

- Final progress reporting (spinner/progress-bar, colors, verbose/quiet semantics).
- Full image pipeline with display of orientation-aware resizing behavior.

Committed the resulting project, which compiles with no external dependencies required beyond the Rust toolchain.
